phases.name: Preflight
phases.summary: Tools, GitHub CLI scopes, installer dry run, build.config.yml, browser sign-ins.

steps.title: Tool versions
steps.detail: git, gh, node, npm, sf (+ code-analyzer), claude, acli, jq, actionlint, shellcheck, specify. Recorded in build-state.md.

steps.title: GitHub CLI and your access
steps.detail: gh auth status needs scopes repo, admin:org, workflow; you need to be an org owner or repo admin.

steps.title: Installer dry run
steps.detail: Shows what install.mjs would add, update or skip, and lists v2 files still in the repo as STALE. Changes nothing.

steps.title: Fill build.config.yml
steps.detail: Org, repo, people per team, runners, Jira, Confluence, sf aliases, Slack. No secrets: the circuit stores none.

steps.title: Sign in to every service in your browser
steps.detail: Sign in once so the later screens open directly.

checklist.text: Signed in to GitHub with an org owner account
Signed in to Atlassian (Jira and Confluence)
Signed in to the DEV and QA orgs
Signed in to Slack and claude.ai

phases.name: GitHub repo, teams, labels
phases.summary: Teams, labels, Actions settings for self-hosted runners, variables; no secrets.

steps.title: Persona teams
steps.detail: Creates architects, developers, testers (closed), adds the people from build.config.yml, gives each team push on the repo. Teams must be disjoint.

steps.title: Labels
steps.detail: plan-review, plan-approved, testplan-approved, ai-ready, ai-generated, ai-attempt-1..3, needs-fix, needs-human, needs-qa, review-room, review-verdict.

steps.title: Actions settings for self-hosted runners
steps.detail: GitHub: self-hosted runners should almost never be used for public repositories. Keep the repo private, never run fork PR workflows, and give workflows read-only tokens by default.

checklist.text: Repository is private (or: public with "Require approval for all external contributors")
Fork pull request workflows: "Run workflows from fork pull requests" is off
Workflow permissions: "Read repository contents and packages permissions"

steps.title: Repository variables
steps.detail: MAX_AI_ATTEMPTS, CIRCUIT_QA_ALIAS, CIRCUIT_PROD_ALIAS, CIRCUIT_RELEASE_ALIAS, DESIGN_PENDING_STATUSES, SLACK_CHANNEL_DEV/QA, CIRCUIT_SLACK_TRANSPORT, SF_AI_TESTER_* from build.config.yml. Names and flags only.

steps.title: No stored credentials
steps.detail: The repository and its environments hold no secrets: no CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, Salesforce JWT keys, Jira tokens or Slack webhooks. Leftovers from v2 can be deleted here.

phases.name: Self-hosted runners
phases.summary: Two runners with their own logins: circuit (PR checks) and circuit-release (deploy-prod).
phases.notes: circuit runner online; release runner not registered yet

steps.title: Register the circuit runner
steps.detail: On the circuit machine, as its service user: download the runner, register it with the labels below and install it as a service.

checklist.text: Runner downloaded from the repository's New self-hosted runner page
Registered with labels self-hosted, circuit
Installed and started as a service

commands: # in the runner folder (downloaded from Settings > Actions > Runners > New self-hosted runner)
notes: The registration token expires after 1 hour; it is read on the runner machine and never stored.
config cannot add labels to a registered runner: change them in Settings > Actions > Runners > the runner > Labels.
This runner holds DEV/QA logins only, never production.

lines: circuit-1: online; labels self-hosted, Linux, circuit

steps.title: Circuit runner logins
steps.detail: As the runner's service user, in a terminal on that machine, sign in once to each tool. Logins stay on the runner; nothing goes into GitHub secrets.

checklist.text: gh signed in (repo, read:org)
claude signed in with a Claude Team seat (and Slack via /mcp if transport is claude)
acli jira auth login --web done
sf logins for the DEV and QA aliases
runner-check.sh prints ok

commands: gh auth login    # scopes repo, read:org
claude           # sign in with the Claude Team seat; then /mcp > Slack if notices use transport claude
sf org login web --alias dev    # or: sf org login device --alias dev on a headless machine
notes: Also install there: sf plugins install @salesforce/plugin-code-analyzer, Node 22, jq, and the SF AI Tester (scripts/ci/install-sf-ai-tester.sh).
Re-run a login when it expires (org refresh, password change).

steps.title: Release runner and the production login
steps.detail: A second machine or service user for deploy-prod only. The person with production rights signs in to the production alias there. Claude and this extension never do.

checklist.text: Registered with labels self-hosted, circuit-release
Installed as a service
Production alias signed in by a person, on this runner only
runner-check.sh prints ok

commands: # in the runner folder (downloaded from Settings > Actions > Runners > New self-hosted runner)
sf org login web --alias prod    # HC-5: a person, on the release runner only
notes: The registration token expires after 1 hour; it is read on the runner machine and never stored.
config cannot add labels to a registered runner: change them in Settings > Actions > Runners > the runner > Labels.
This runner holds the one login to the production alias and runs deploy-prod only.

result.text: [self-hosted, circuit-release]: no runner registered with these labels

phases.name: Salesforce logins
phases.summary: Each person logs in to DEV and QA with their own user; no integration users, no JWT keys.

steps.title: Log in to DEV and QA
steps.detail: sf org login web --alias dev and --alias qa. Any connected org may be DEV or QA (sandbox, scratch, Developer Edition, demo org).
steps.action: Open terminal: sf org login web

actions.label: Open terminal: sf org login web

steps.title: Org aliases
steps.detail: sf org display for dev and qa, and no production alias (prod, production, live) on this machine. Architects may hold it for manual work; AI is still blocked by the guard.

phases.name: Repo foundation
phases.summary: Installer on pipeline/foundation; persona MCP URLs; PR merged by a person.

steps.title: Branch pipeline/foundation
steps.detail: git switch -c pipeline/foundation (or switch to it).

steps.title: Run the installer
steps.detail: install.mjs for real: CLAUDE.md, .claude/, CODEOWNERS, PR template, scripts/ci, .coderabbit.yaml, sf-config, build.config.yml, build-state.md. Existing files are skipped; workflows wait for B9.

steps.title: Persona MCP URLs
steps.detail: Replaces VERIFY placeholders in .claude/personas/*.mcp.json with the vendor URLs (Atlassian v2, Lucid, Fireflies, GitHub, Slack). Sign-in is OAuth in Claude (/mcp), never a key.

steps.title: Commit, push and merge the foundation PR
steps.detail: Commit everything except .github/workflows/, push pipeline/foundation, open the PR. A person merges it.

checklist.text: Committed without .github/workflows/
PR opened
PR merged by a person

phases.name: Spec Kit
phases.summary: The Architect's local drafting scaffold: specify init + spec-kit-sf; .specify/specs stays out of git.

steps.title: specify init
steps.detail: specify init --here --integration claude --integration-options=--no-model-invocation

steps.title: spec-kit-sf extension
steps.detail: specify extension add sf --from the v2.0.1 release archive (confirm the URL in the terminal).

steps.title: Remove deploy skills
steps.detail: Deletes .claude/skills/speckit-sf-deploy, -hotfix and -pr (the guard blocks them anyway).

steps.title: Spec Kit state
steps.detail: .specify/, extension sf, .specify/specs/ gitignored (specs are published to Confluence and Jira), production alias named in sf-config.

steps.title: Constitution
steps.detail: An Architect runs /speckit-sf-constitution against dev and appends the house rules as Article X; the Architect reviews and merges the PR.

checklist.text: Constitution generated
Article X added
PR merged by the Architect

phases.name: Jira and acli
phases.summary: Atlassian CLI web login, Jira groups/fields/workflows, GitHub for Atlassian.

steps.title: Atlassian CLI login
steps.detail: acli covers Jira (the official reference has no Confluence commands). Sign in with the browser: acli jira auth login --web, then pick the site. Never the --token form. Each acli version is supported for 6 months: keep it updated.
steps.action: Open terminal: acli jira auth login --web
commands: curl -LO https://acli.atlassian.com/linux/latest/acli_linux_amd64/acli && chmod +x acli && sudo mv acli /usr/local/bin/

actions.label: Open terminal: acli jira auth login --web

steps.title: Groups, fields and workflows
steps.detail: Jira admin, in the browser: groups architects/developers/testers; company-managed project; fields; epic workflow with Approve design restricted to architects; story workflow with Ready for Dev restricted to testers (G2).

checklist.text: Groups match the GitHub teams
Fields: Design page, Approved design version, Acceptance criteria, Story type, Schema change, Persona, Test level, AC id, Testability confirmed
Epic: Backlog > Design Review > Approve design (architects only, sets Approved design version) > Design Approved
Story: Backlog > Ready for Dev (testers only, Testability confirmed, label ai-ready) > In Build > Code Review > QA > Done
No Jira automation calls GitHub and no PAT in any rule

steps.title: GitHub for Atlassian
steps.detail: Jira > Apps > Explore more apps > GitHub for Atlassian > Get app; a Jira site admin and a GitHub org owner connect the org. Branches feature/<KEY>-<slug> and PR titles "<KEY> ..." then link to the work item.

checklist.text: App installed in Jira
GitHub org connected
A test branch with an uppercase key shows in the work item's Development panel

steps.title: Jira field ids
steps.detail: .specify/extensions/jira/jira-config.json (field ids for Design page and Approved design version), built once by arch-jira-push and committed; design-gate reads it on the runner.

phases.name: Confluence and MCP sign-ins
phases.summary: Approved page status, edit restriction for architects, Lucid; Atlassian, Lucid and Fireflies MCP via /mcp.

steps.title: Design space and Approved status
steps.detail: A space admin adds Approved as a suggested content status. Confluence cannot limit status changes to a group, so restrict edit of approved design pages to the architects group; the circuit checks who set Approved from the page history.

checklist.text: Space exists (confluence.space_key)
Approved is a suggested content status
Approved design pages: edit restricted to architects
Lucid for Confluence installed

steps.title: MCP sign-ins (Atlassian, Lucid, Fireflies)
steps.detail: Each person, in an interactive Claude session: /mcp and sign in to atlassian (Rovo MCP, OAuth). Architects also sign in to lucid and fireflies. claude -p cannot run the OAuth flow, so this happens interactively first. No API-token auth.

checklist.text: atlassian signed in
lucid signed in (Architects)
fireflies signed in (Architects)

phases.name: Slack and the review room
phases.summary: Gate channels, #review-room, Claude Slack connector, GitHub app for Slack; no webhooks.

steps.title: Slack workspace
steps.detail: A Slack admin approves the Claude Slack connector (claude.ai > Connectors > Slack), installs the GitHub app for Slack, and invites CodeRabbit and Claude to the review room. No incoming webhook, no bot token.

checklist.text: Channels #arch-gate, #dev-gate, #qa-gate, #review-room exist
Claude Slack connector approved for the workspace
GitHub app for Slack subscribed
CodeRabbit and Claude invited to #review-room

steps.title: Slack MCP sign-in
steps.detail: Each person (and the circuit runner's service user when transport is claude) signs in to Slack once in an interactive Claude session (/mcp).

checklist.text: Signed in to Slack in Claude
A test message posted and read in #review-room

phases.name: Workflows and CodeRabbit
phases.summary: The five v3 workflows on pipeline/workflows, actionlint and shellcheck clean, CodeRabbit on this repo.

steps.title: Branch pipeline/workflows
steps.detail: git switch -c pipeline/workflows (or switch to it).

steps.title: actionlint and shellcheck
steps.detail: actionlint on .github/workflows/*.yml (custom runner labels in .github/actionlint.yaml) and shellcheck on scripts/ci/*.sh must be clean. No workflow reads a stored credential.

steps.title: CodeRabbit repository access
steps.detail: Install the CodeRabbit GitHub App with access to this repository. Its reviews appear as review signals on every PR, and it joins the review room in Slack.

checklist.text: CodeRabbit installed with access to this repository

steps.title: Workflows PR
steps.detail: Push pipeline/workflows and open the PR; the Architect merges it (CODEOWNERS covers .github/).

checklist.text: pr-checks, design-gate, persona-gates, fix-router, deploy-prod visible in Actions
Self-hosted jobs ran on circuit for a same-repo test PR
CodeRabbit commented on the PR
Merged by the Architect

steps.title: Rulesets for main
steps.detail: circuit-main-gates (PRs, code owners, required checks guard static code-analyzer qa design-gate gate/*) and circuit-merge-architects-only. You review both payloads before they are created.

steps.title: Production reviewers
steps.detail: Environment production: required reviewers = team architects, prevent self-review, deployments from main only. deploy-prod runs on circuit-release.

phases.name: Persona workstations
phases.summary: Every person: this extension, the plugin, their logins and MCP sign-ins.

steps.title: Each person connects
steps.detail: Each person installs this extension and the plugin, runs scripts/setup-persona.sh, and checks Connections: GitHub, Claude, sf, acli, Atlassian MCP, Fireflies MCP (Architects), Slack MCP, runner online.

checklist.text: Architects connected
Developers connected
Testers connected
Each ran a first command

phases.name: Dry run
phases.summary: One made-up feature through every step, every persona, every app (HC-10).

steps.title: Dry-run settings
steps.detail: DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT=production-dryrun (an environment whose CIRCUIT_RELEASE_ALIAS is the QA alias) and FIX_ROUTER_DRY_RUN=false. The person also signs the release runner in to QA for the dry run, and out afterwards.

steps.title: Run the circuit end to end
steps.detail: One made-up feature (Jira label dryrun) through the v3 flow with people at every gate.

checklist.text: Source added; Confluence design page with Decisions and Org snapshot
G1 by an architect at version N
Epic, Story 00 and stories with Approved design version N; a second push creates nothing
Test cases per AC in Jira; G2
Start story creates feature/<KEY>-<slug> and a draft PR
Tester adds tests to the PR; G3/G4 by the right teams
Removing a // TC: reference fails static
Re-approving the design at N+1 fails design-gate
A forced failure gives needs-fix, then needs-human after 3 attempts
A blocked AI-tester case gives needs-qa
Review room thread and verdict on the PR
Merge is architect-only; deploy waits for approval and runs on circuit-release

steps.title: Clean up
steps.detail: Removes DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT so deploys target production again. Close dry-run issues and delete branches yourself; keep the PRs as evidence.

phases.name: Go live
phases.summary: One small real feature; retro per persona; mark the bootstrap COMPLETE.

steps.title: First real feature
steps.detail: One small real feature. Claude only watches and reports; people act at every gate. Then a retro per persona.

checklist.text: Feature delivered through every gate
Retro notes folded into constitution, CLAUDE.md, .coderabbit.yaml and test conventions
